analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1254-1648, historical release notes). The PR patch adds a v0.10.1 candidate section at the head of the file (head lines 11-151). That section is only partly visible, and only in a truncated patch excerpt, so I could not examine the head-side text and make no claims about it. The base excerpts are documentation only. They change no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing behavior.

The visible patch excerpt states two rollout dependencies. First, the provider release should run behind a coordinator containing darkbloom-platform#411, which refuses logprobs on certain models. Second, page-cache accounting changes load admission and KV budgets for every model. These are operational notes that touch availability and the memory-admission assumptions behind T-029 and TB-007. They are not security regressions in themselves, and the code behind them is not in the supplied evidence. The libs/mlx-swift-lm pin bump (7bed8216 to 6148b6da) is likewise unreviewable here. Reviewers of the code files should check that the page-cache accounting change does not weaken memory safeguards, and that the GLM logprob groundwork stays disabled.

The base text mentions T-041 and SEC-035 changes (the 30-minute TTL and the SSD write budget raised to 750 GB/day). Those are pre-existing entries and are unchanged by this PR as far as the visible evidence shows. I identified no concrete security regression and no threat-model drift from the supplied units. I set needs_deeper_review=true because the head-side changelog content and the related code changes were not supplied.
